title: Compact operators and the spectrum
summary: Compact subsets of a Hilbert space; finite-rank operators and their norm limits; compact operators; the spectrum and resolvent of a bounded operator.

objectives.description: Characterise compact diagonal operators and explain approximation by finite rank in Hilbert space.
Use the Neumann series to bound the resolvent and prove invertibility is an open condition.
Distinguish spectrum from eigenvalues by constructing an approximate eigenvector sequence.

preparation.description: Read Lectures 19–20 of the 18.102 Spring 2021 notes.

activities.title: Lecture and exact source reading

exitCheck.description: Use the whole problem sheet to sample the listed objectives. Give an independent account of the main theorem and its hypotheses, and solve the transfer/synthesis task. An accepted single exercise is evidence only for its tested capabilities, not whole-unit mastery.

commonMisconceptions.claim: The spectrum consists only of eigenvalues.
commonMisconceptions.correction: An operator can fail surjectivity or a bounded-inverse estimate without a nonzero kernel. The compact diagonal 1/n has zero in its spectrum but not as an eigenvalue.

commonMisconceptions.claim: A pointwise limit of finite-rank operators must be compact.
commonMisconceptions.correction: The convergence must be in operator norm; finite-coordinate projections converge pointwise to the noncompact identity.
